messages:
jess: Heads-up — hitting a weird TS typing collapse when using the JS SDK from an edge runtime (Deno/Cloudflare/edge-worker). Generics on the client call end up as `any` at callsite. Anyone seen this?

sam: yep saw similar. Usually it's an ESM/CJS interop + tsconfig/moduleResolution quirk. Can you paste the import and tsconfig?

jess: import is `import Redwood from '@redwood/inference'` (default). Call looks like `const r = new Redwood<ClientSchema>(); r.request(...)` and TS stops inferring ClientSchema, becomes `any`. tsconfig:```json
{
  "compilerOptions": {
    "target": "ES2020",
    "module": "ESNext",
    "moduleResolution": "node",
    "esModuleInterop": true,
    "skipLibCheck": true,
    "strict": true
  }
}
```

kai: a few things to try: 1) switch moduleResolution to "bundler" for edge builds (helps with ESM-only packages), 2) prefer `import type` for types, 3) check the SDK's package.json "exports"/"types" layout — sometimes the types entry points are CJS-only and tsc falls back.

marco: +1 on moduleResolution=bundler. Also try changing import to named import if available: `import { RedwoodClient } from '@redwood/inference'` — default export interop can erase generics with esModuleInterop toggles.

jess: tried named import, still fuzzy. If I `const r = new (Redwood as any)()`, types are gone (obviously). But even with `as typeof Redwood`, inference fails.

elaine: quick repro I had before: when a package re-exports a generic type through a compiled ESM entry that uses `export =` under the hood (or has mixed cjs artifacts), TS will widen to `any`. Workarounds: - ensure SDK ships `.d.ts` for the ESM export path, - add a types-only entry (`exports.{ "types": "./dist/index.d.ts" }`).

sam: another angle — if the edge bundler (esbuild/webpack/rollup) is set to transform or strip `export type` or inline too aggressively, the type linking breaks. For Deno/edge, toolchains sometimes drop type-only exports. Are you bundling or using native ESM?

jess: bundling with esbuild for the edge bundle. We set target chrome120/deno. Not stripping types intentionally.

kai: try this quick local test: create a tiny file using `import type` to pull the generic and then re-export it as `type`. e.g.```ts
// foo.ts
import type { ClientSchema } from '@redwood/inference';
export type Schema = ClientSchema;
```
If your consumer can see `Schema` correctly then the SDK's types are present but the default import path is the problem.

marco: also check package.json of SDK for `typesVersions` — some packages use that to map TS versions and ESM consumers might hit a different path. If the SDK's dts were emitted with `declare class Redwood<T = any>` then consumers will get `any` unless the dts is generic-correct.

jess: interesting — I inspected node_modules/@redwood/inference/package.json. Exports: {".": {"import": "./dist/esm/index.js", "require": "./dist/cjs/index.js", "types": "./dist/index.d.ts"}} Types file exists but the dts seems to re-export from `./types/generated` which is a .d.ts that uses `export =` patterns.

elaine: ok that explains it. `export =` + ESM import interop will break generic inference. Short-term fixes: 1) ask SDK to add a pure ESM types entry (no `export =`), 2) in your app, consume named types directly with `import type { RedwoodClient } from '@redwood/inference/dist/types'` (not ideal), or 3) explicitly annotate generics at callsite as a bandaid: `new Redwood<MySchema>()` (you already do but inference still lost?).

jess: I did explicit generic on `new Redwood<ClientSchema>()` — callsite still shows `any` for `r.request` parameter types.

sam: that suggests the runtime class declaration in d.ts lacks the generic constraint on methods (e.g., methods typed as `any`). Can you grep the d.ts for `request<T` and see signature?

jess: grep shows `request(...args: any[]): Promise<any>` in the built d.ts. So packaging bug.

marco: filing an issue on the SDK repo is warranted. Dev-bot: please create issue in redwood-js/sdk repo with label dx/typing and link this thread.

dev-bot: Created issue #4521: "SDK: request method types widened to any in published d.ts (edge/ESM consumers)" — https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/issues/4521 :robot_face:

elaine: next steps: 1) SDK team needs to re-run dts generation keeping generics across entrypoints (skip `export =` style re-exports), 2) add CI test that installs the package in a simple ESM/edge project and checks that a small TS compile preserves types, 3) add a short migration note for consumers (if they rely on named imports as a workaround).

jess: thanks all — I have a repro and an issue. For our app I'll pin a patch using a local patch-package to restore types until upstream fix. Appreciate the quick triage :thumbsup:
